aSessionKeepsATool: A session keeps a tool process (100–250MB of memory) once you send a message. When it has been idle past the set time, or more processes are open than the limit (least recently used first), the process stops; the chat stays, and the next message resumes the same session (startup takes a few seconds). Sessions that are replying are never stopped. Terminal-mode sessions are not managed by these settings; use "Stop Process" in the session menu when done.
runTerminalSessionsInTmux: Run terminal sessions in tmux so they survive daemon restarts and upgrades, and reconnect when opened (needs tmux 3.2+; not supported on Windows)
continueAfterUsageLimitsWhen: Continue after usage limits: when Claude Code or Codex stops on its usage limit in the chat UI, send "continue" automatically once the limit resets (not when it resets more than a day out, or after hitting the limit several times in a row)
lookedUpOnPathAnd: Looked up on PATH and common install locations. Set a path here to pin a version.
shownUnderTheSessionInput: Shown under the session input. Use built-in fields, a command (same idea as Claude Code statusLine), or both. Applies only to sessions on this host.
runsInTheSessionDirectory: Runs in the session directory. stdin is JSON (session_id, cwd, model, workspace, cost, context_window, plus tool, usage, git under yi_console). The first output line is shown, ANSI colors included. Over 3 seconds counts as failure. On Windows it runs via cmd.
whenNoCommandIsSet: When no command is set, Claude Code sessions use statusLine from ~/.claude/settings.json (Git Bash on Windows)
savedCommandsForThisHost: Saved commands for this host. Type / at the start of any session input to insert one, then edit it. Stored on this machine’s yi-agentd, so phones and computers share them.
